FirstAlert relays the information of the Japan Meteorological Agency through unofficial services, and can be late or miss it. Follow the official information and the instructions of your municipality.

Get out of the water and away from the shore.
Colours show the strongest intensity in each prefecture. ✕ is the epicentre, ◉ your place.
Red circle: strong shaking (S wave). Blue circle: first tremor (P wave). ✕ is the epicentre, ◉ your place.

With your area, warnings for other areas of your prefecture are not taken for yours. With the whole prefecture, every area of it counts as yours, which may alert more often, but never less.

Training reports are shown quietly, never as real ones.
Each alert is told in several ways at once, so that it reaches everyone: in words on the screen, in colour and in shape, by sound, by voice, by vibration and by light.
Each level has its own tones.
Emergencies sound as an alarm, also when the phone is silenced.
A pattern of its own for each level.
Flashes the camera light during emergencies, for anyone who may not hear the sound. Less than three flashes a second.

A test alert at the chosen level, with everything turned on above. It says that it is a test.
The words of the alerts, the voice, and the screens. The names of places are always in Japanese, as the Japan Meteorological Agency gives them.
Short sentences and easy words, with readings of the harder ones.

FirstAlert is not provided by the Japan Meteorological Agency or any government. It receives their information through unofficial relays, which can be late, wrong or stop. Never rely on it alone: follow the official information, the emergency broadcasts and the instructions of your municipality.

Earthquake early warnings, earthquake, tsunami and special information: the Japan Meteorological Agency, relayed by the Wolfx Project (Wolfx Open API) and P2P Quake (P2P地震情報 JSON API v2).\nNames of the areas: the Japan Meteorological Agency.\nOutlines of the prefectures: Natural Earth (public domain).
